plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: An epiphytic cactus with segmented, flattened stems and tubular flowers with pointed, claw-like segments on the stem edges. Widely grown as a houseplant, it is triggered to bloom by long nights and cool temperatures.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (November to January in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil; cultivated worldwide as a houseplant
plants.funFact: Unlike desert cacti, it grows on trees in humid Brazilian forests, and it can live for decades, with some plants passed down through families for generations.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and delicate, often fragrant flowers that open from autumn into early winter. It is more sun-tolerant and earlier blooming than the common camellia.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to Japan and southern China; widely grown in the southeastern United States, Mediterranean Europe, Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua seeds are pressed to produce camellia oil, used for centuries in Japan for cooking and hair care.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, deciduous to semi-evergreen tree with fern-like foliage that produces dense clusters of trumpet-shaped violet-blue flowers, blanketing streets and the ground beneath in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; commonly seen in Australia, South Africa, Argentina and Brazil
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, tens of thousands of jacarandas bloom at this time, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City,' and in Australia, a folk belief says a flower falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum morifolium
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial with a huge diversity of flower forms, from daisy-like to large pompons. Short days trigger flowering, and it is among the last garden flowers to bloom before winter in temperate regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November, lingering into early December in mild climates)
plants.location: Native to East Asia; cultivated worldwide in gardens and commercial greenhouses
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are celebrated in Japan with an annual Chrysanthemum Festival, and the flower is the emblem of the Imperial family and its throne.
